findings.text: — `_run_index_path` builds a per-project SQLite cache `ledger-<hash>.sqlite` that `load` already consults (via `_indexed_data`, `use_index=True`), rebuilding it from the files when stale; the plan's entire §2 model ("files are authority, the index is a disposable cache rebuilt when it misses") is this mechanism, yet the plan calls only `run_store.db` "the index" and never names this cache.

— the plan demotes `~/.config/reckon/crew/run_store.db` to "an index ... never committed ... rebuilt from the files", but that store is already read by `reckon/budget.py:509,545` (`RunStore`), `reckon/crew/carryover_census.py:450`, `reckon/crew/death_census.py:172` and written by `reckon/crew/promotion.py:2395` (`import_ledger`), so the plan's claim "today a shadow nothing reads" is false.

— the rule that two copies of one run count once only when their canonical serialisations agree, and that a disagreement refuses the whole read naming the id and both paths, is implemented twice: in `_indexed_data`'s SQL conflict query (`ledger.py:962-982`) and again in `load`'s uncached union (`ledger.py:1081-1085`), each with its own comparison.

— the read side is a single `load` with two boolean modes (`use_index`, `headers_only`), a second `_indexed_data(picker_only=)` mode, and a `picker_runs` entry point (`ledger.py:842`) that bypasses `load` and falls back to it — four caller-selected projections over the same machinery.

— `index_lag` is defined as "the number of run files whose id is absent from the index", computed against `run_store.indexed_run_ids` while the reader-side cache (`_run_index_path`) is untouched; the plan offers no mapping of the two index families and no search result showing the store's prior-art consumers.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the reader surface is spread across one function with three boolean modes plus a bypass path over two caches, rather than one deep `load` that hides the index choice.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan names `run_store.db` as "the index" but a second SQLite cache over the same rows already backs `load`, and the union/conflict invariant is implemented twice.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched `reckon/ledger.py` and `reckon/run_store.py` and cites the serialiser and `DETAIL_FIELDS`, but its premise that `run_store.db` is "a shadow nothing reads" is false and it never maps the store's existing consumers, so the "index" it demotes already has readers whose contract it changes.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no unjustified thin wrapper was found.
